# tiny-dist-audit

> Deterministic release-artifact manifests and drift detection for Python
> wheels, sdists, and directory trees. Zero dependencies, pure stdlib, one module.

## What it does
- build_manifest(path) -> JSON manifest with file count, per-file sha256,
  metadata (name, version, requires_python, license_expression, requires_dist),
  and a canonical tree_digest.
- check(path, baseline, key=..., fail_on=...) -> report with drift, risky
  credential-shaped paths, signature state, severity, and reasons.
- diff_manifests(old, new) -> added / removed / changed files and metadata fields.
- sign(manifest, key) / verify(manifest, key) -> HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical body.

## Facts an agent needs
- Manifest schema string: `tiny-dist-audit/1` (`MANIFEST_SCHEMA`).
- Python 3.9+. No dependencies. CLI entry point: `dist-audit`.
- `dist-audit check ARTIFACT --baseline M.json --fail-on high` exits 5 on drift.
- Exit codes: 0 clean, 2 usage/unreadable, 4 diff found differences, 5 check failed.
- Severity: changed/removed file = high, added file = medium, metadata = low,
  credential-shaped path = high, INVALID signature = critical.
- Manifests are byte-stable across rebuilds; commit them and diff per tag.
- The leak scan only inspects path NAMES; it cannot see a secret inside a .py file.
- HMAC signing proves the manifest was not hand-edited. It is NOT Sigstore and
  does not bind build identity to the artifact.

- Source: https://github.com/hussain-alsaibai/tiny-dist-audit
- Example CI gate: examples/release-gate.yml
